stem: Why are people considered the ultimate resource of a nation?
options: They turn other materials into resources through their skills and knowledge
They reduce the value of resources
solution: Human resources are the ultimate resource because people's skill, knowledge and ability make natural materials useful and drive all development.

stem: The number of people living per unit area (e.g. per square kilometre) is called:
solution: Population density is the number of persons living per square kilometre of land.

stem: Which of the following is a geographical factor affecting population distribution?
solution: Geographical factors like relief, climate, soil, water and minerals strongly influence where people live.

stem: People tend to live in large numbers in areas with:
solution: Fertile plains with adequate water and a moderate climate support dense populations, while mountains, deserts and dense forests are sparsely populated.

stem: Which of the following is a densely populated region of the world?
options: The Indo-Gangetic plains of South Asia
solution: The Indo-Gangetic plains, along with parts of East Asia and Europe, are among the world's most densely populated regions.

stem: The change in the number of people in a region over time is called:
solution: Population change refers to the increase or decrease in the number of people over a period of time.

stem: Population change is determined by births, deaths and:
solution: The three factors that change population are births (birth rate), deaths (death rate) and migration.

stem: The number of live births per 1,000 people in a year is called the:
solution: The birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 people per year.

stem: The number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year is called the:
solution: The death rate is the number of deaths per 1,000 people per year.

stem: The difference between the birth rate and the death rate is called the:
solution: The natural growth rate is the difference between the birth rate and the death rate.

stem: The movement of people into a country is called:
solution: Immigration is when people move into a country; emigration is when they move out of a country.

stem: The movement of people out of a country is called:
solution: Emigration refers to people leaving a country to settle elsewhere; those who move in are immigrants.

stem: The most common type of internal migration in developing countries is from:
solution: Rural-to-urban migration, in search of jobs and better facilities, is the most common form of internal migration.

stem: The world's population crossed the 7 billion mark around:
solution: The world population reached about 7 billion around 2011, having grown rapidly in the twentieth century.

stem: The rapid rise in world population in recent times is mainly due to:
options: A fall in death rates while birth rates remained relatively high
A fall in birth rates only
solution: Better healthcare, food and sanitation lowered death rates while birth rates stayed high, causing rapid population growth.

stem: The structure of a population in terms of age and sex is shown by a(n):
solution: A population pyramid (age-sex pyramid) shows the distribution of a population across age groups and by sex.

stem: The number of females per 1,000 males in a population is called the:
solution: The sex ratio expresses the number of females per 1,000 males (in some countries per 100 males).

stem: In a population pyramid, the working-age group is usually taken as those aged:
solution: The working-age (economically active) group is generally taken as 15-65 years; below 15 are children and above 65 are the aged.

stem: The proportion of literate people in a population is measured by the:
solution: The literacy rate measures the percentage of people (usually above a certain age) who can read and write.

stem: Which of the following is a social or economic factor affecting population distribution?
options: Availability of jobs, housing and education
solution: Social/economic/cultural factors like jobs, housing, education and industrialisation draw people to certain areas, affecting distribution.

stem: The three main groups into which a population's age composition is divided are children, the aged and the:
solution: Age composition is divided into children (below 15), the working-age group (15-65) and the aged (above 65).

stem: A country with a large proportion of children in its population is likely to have a:
solution: A wide base in the population pyramid (many children) indicates a high birth rate.

stem: Sparsely populated regions of the world typically include:
options: Deserts, high mountains and dense forests
solution: Areas with harsh climates or difficult terrain — deserts, high mountains and dense forests — are sparsely populated.

stem: Why does the availability of minerals attract population to a region?
options: Mining and related industries create jobs, drawing people
solution: The presence of minerals leads to mining and industries, which create employment and attract people to settle there.

stem: The average density of population of the world (around the time of the chapter) was approximately:
solution: The world's average population density was about 51 persons per square kilometre.

stem: Which continent has a very small population despite its large size, due to its extreme cold?
solution: Antarctica, being extremely cold and ice-covered, has no permanent population despite its large area.

stem: Migration affects the population of a place by:
solution: Migration changes population size: immigration adds to a region's population, while emigration reduces it.

stem: Better healthcare and food supply in the modern era have mainly led to:
options: A decline in death rates and longer life expectancy
solution: Improved healthcare, nutrition and sanitation reduced death rates and increased life expectancy, contributing to population growth.

stem: The composition of a population refers to its structure in terms of:
solution: Population composition describes the structure of a population by age, sex, literacy, occupation, income and other characteristics.

stem: A place is likely to be densely populated if it has:
options: Fertile soil, adequate water, a good climate and job opportunities
solution: Favourable conditions — fertile soil, water, a pleasant climate and economic opportunities — attract dense settlement.

stem: The 'occupational structure' of a population refers to the:
options: Distribution of workers among different types of jobs
solution: Occupational structure shows how the working population is distributed among primary, secondary and tertiary activities.

stem: Countries in the primary occupations sector have a large share of workers in:
solution: A high share of workers in agriculture, mining, fishing and forestry indicates a predominance of primary occupations.

stem: As countries develop, the share of the working population tends to shift towards:
options: Secondary and tertiary (industry and services) sectors
solution: With development, workers move from agriculture (primary) into industry (secondary) and services (tertiary).

stem: The three most densely populated areas of the world are found in:
options: South Asia, East Asia and parts of Europe
solution: South Asia, East Asia and Western/Central Europe contain some of the most densely populated areas of the world.

stem: A high natural growth rate occurs when:
options: The birth rate is much higher than the death rate
The death rate is higher than the birth rate
solution: When births greatly exceed deaths, the natural growth rate is high, causing population to increase rapidly.

stem: Human resource development means improving the:
options: Health, education and skills of people
solution: Developing human resources means investing in people's health, education and skills so they can contribute more effectively.

stem: Which of the following would reduce the quality of human resources?
options: Poor health, illiteracy and lack of skills
solution: Ill health, illiteracy and a lack of skills reduce the productivity and quality of human resources.

stem: The distribution of the world's population is best described as:
options: Uneven, with some areas very crowded and others nearly empty
solution: Population is very unevenly distributed — some regions are densely crowded while vast areas remain sparsely populated.

stem: A wide-based population pyramid indicates:
options: A large number of young people and a high birth rate
Equal numbers in all age groups
solution: A pyramid with a broad base shows many children and a high birth rate, typical of a young, growing population.

stem: A narrow-based population pyramid usually indicates:
options: Low birth rates and an ageing population
solution: A narrow base reflects fewer children (low birth rate) and a larger proportion of older people, typical of developed, ageing societies.

stem: Which of the following statements about population growth is correct?
options: It results from the combined effect of births, deaths and migration
It depends only on the weather
It is fixed and never changes
It depends only on the number of rivers
solution: Population growth is the net result of births, deaths and migration in a region.

stem: The 'quality' of population is reflected in indicators such as:
options: Literacy rate, health and skill levels
solution: Population quality is indicated by literacy, health, life expectancy and skill levels of the people.

stem: Which of the following regions is likely to be sparsely populated?
solution: The high Himalayas, with rugged terrain and a harsh climate, are sparsely populated, unlike fertile plains and river valleys.

stem: Population is a resource, but very rapid population growth can:
options: Put pressure on resources and services like food, housing and jobs
solution: Rapid population growth can strain resources and services (food, housing, healthcare, jobs), posing challenges to development.

stem: Improved education and healthcare turn a large population into:
solution: With education, health and skills, a large population becomes a valuable, productive human resource rather than a burden.

stem: The birth rate and death rate are usually expressed per:
solution: Both birth rate and death rate are conventionally expressed per 1,000 people per year.

stem: Which of the following factors would attract migrants to a city?
options: Better jobs, education and healthcare (pull factors)
solution: Pull factors like better jobs, education, healthcare and amenities attract migrants to cities.

stem: Factors that force people to leave a place, such as unemployment or drought, are called:
solution: Push factors (e.g. unemployment, poverty, natural disasters) drive people away from a place, while pull factors attract them elsewhere.

stem: Which of the following is the correct relationship?
options: Natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate
Natural growth rate = birth rate + death rate
solution: The natural growth rate equals the birth rate minus the death rate.

stem: Factors that pull people towards a place (migration) include:
options: Better job opportunities, education and living conditions
solution: PULL factors ATTRACT migrants — BETTER JOBS, EDUCATION, and LIVING CONDITIONS. Unemployment, drought, and war are push factors. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Factors that push people away from a place include:
options: Unemployment, poor living conditions, drought and natural disasters
solution: PUSH factors DRIVE people AWAY — UNEMPLOYMENT, POOR conditions, DROUGHT, and DISASTERS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Match List-I with List-II: P. Birth rate Q. Death rate R. Migration S. Natural growth rate | 1. Deaths per 1000 per year 2. Difference between birth and death rates 3. Births per 1000 per year 4. Movement of people in/out
solution: Birth rate → births per 1000 (P-3); Death rate → deaths per 1000 (Q-1); Migration → movement in/out (R-4); Natural growth rate → birth minus death rate (S-2). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The three most densely populated regions of the world include:
options: South and East Asia, Europe, and north-eastern USA
solution: The most densely populated regions are SOUTH and EAST ASIA, EUROPE, and NORTH-EASTERN USA. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): River valleys and fertile plains are densely populated. Reason (R): They offer fertile soil, water and flat land suitable for farming and settlement. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — river valleys are densely populated. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: they offer FERTILE SOIL, WATER, and FLAT LAND for farming and settlement. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The world's two most populous countries are:
solution: INDIA and CHINA are the world's two MOST POPULOUS countries. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following environments discourages large populations?
options: Hot, dry deserts like the Sahara
solution: HOT, DRY DESERTS like the SAHARA discourage large populations due to lack of water and harsh conditions. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The rapid growth of world population since the 1800s is largely due to:
options: Falling death rates from better healthcare, food and sanitation
solution: World population grew rapidly mainly because DEATH RATES FELL due to BETTER HEALTHCARE, FOOD, and SANITATION, while birth rates stayed high. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The age-sex structure of a population is graphically shown by a:
solution: The AGE-SEX structure of a population is shown by a POPULATION PYRAMID. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A population pyramid with a wide base indicates:
options: A high proportion of children and high birth rate
solution: A WIDE-BASED pyramid shows a HIGH proportion of CHILDREN and a HIGH BIRTH RATE (a young, growing population). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A population pyramid with a narrow base and wider middle/top indicates:
options: A low birth rate and an ageing population
solution: A NARROW-BASED pyramid shows a LOW BIRTH RATE and an AGEING population. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The sex ratio is the number of:
solution: In India's usage, the SEX RATIO is the number of FEMALES per 1000 MALES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The working-age group in a population is usually taken as those aged:
solution: The WORKING-AGE group is usually 15 to 59 (or 64) YEARS. Below 15 and above 60 are dependents. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The ratio of dependents (children and elderly) to the working-age population is called the:
solution: The DEPENDENCY RATIO is the ratio of DEPENDENTS (children + elderly) to the WORKING-AGE population. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. A large youthful population is called a demographic dividend if productively employed. 2. It becomes a burden if there are not enough jobs. Which is/are correct?
solution: BOTH are correct: a large YOUTHFUL population is a DEMOGRAPHIC DIVIDEND if PRODUCTIVELY EMPLOYED (1), but a BURDEN if there are NOT ENOUGH JOBS (2). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The percentage of literate people aged 7 and above is the:
solution: The LITERACY RATE is the percentage of LITERATE people (usually aged 7 and above). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Human resource development is essential. Reason (R): Investing in education, health and skills turns a large population into a productive workforce. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — human resource development is essential. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: INVESTING in EDUCATION, HEALTH, and SKILLS turns a large population into a PRODUCTIVE workforce. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The occupational structure of a population refers to:
options: The distribution of workers among primary, secondary and tertiary activities
solution: OCCUPATIONAL STRUCTURE is the distribution of WORKERS among PRIMARY, SECONDARY, and TERTIARY activities. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In developing countries, a large share of the workforce is engaged in:
solution: In DEVELOPING countries, a LARGE share of workers is in PRIMARY activities, especially AGRICULTURE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: As a country develops, the share of workers usually shifts from:
options: Primary to secondary and tertiary sectors
solution: With DEVELOPMENT, the workforce shifts from PRIMARY (agriculture) to SECONDARY (industry) and TERTIARY (services) sectors. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Immigration is the movement of people ______ a country, and emigration is the movement ______ a country.
solution: IMMIGRATION is movement INTO a country; EMIGRATION is movement OUT OF a country. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The most common form of internal migration in developing countries is from:
solution: The most common INTERNAL migration in developing countries is RURAL to URBAN (in search of jobs). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Immigration — moving in 2. Emigration — moving out 3. Internal migration — within a country. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE match: IMMIGRATION → moving in; EMIGRATION → moving out; INTERNAL MIGRATION → within a country. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Population density is calculated as:
options: Total population divided by total area
solution: POPULATION DENSITY = TOTAL POPULATION ÷ TOTAL AREA (people per sq km). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which continent is very sparsely populated because of its extremely cold climate?
solution: ANTARCTICA is very SPARSELY populated (essentially no permanent population) due to its EXTREMELY COLD climate. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following social factors attracts people to settle in an area?
options: Availability of good education, healthcare and housing
solution: Good EDUCATION, HEALTHCARE, and HOUSING are SOCIAL factors that ATTRACT settlement. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which economic factor attracts population to a region?
solution: The availability of JOBS and INDUSTRIES is an ECONOMIC factor attracting population. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Very rapid population growth can strain resources. Reason (R): More people require more food, water, housing, and services, which limited resources may not meet. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — rapid growth strains resources. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: MORE PEOPLE need more FOOD, WATER, HOUSING, and SERVICES, straining LIMITED resources. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Life expectancy refers to:
options: The average number of years a person is expected to live
The number of births per year
solution: LIFE EXPECTANCY is the AVERAGE number of YEARS a person is expected to LIVE, an indicator of population quality and health. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Rising life expectancy in a country usually reflects:
options: Improved healthcare, nutrition and living standards
solution: RISING LIFE EXPECTANCY reflects IMPROVED healthcare, NUTRITION, and LIVING STANDARDS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The quality of a population is reflected in indicators such as:
options: Literacy rate, health/life expectancy and skill levels
solution: Population QUALITY is reflected in LITERACY, HEALTH/LIFE EXPECTANCY, and SKILL levels. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A country where the death rate exceeds the birth rate will experience:
solution: If the DEATH RATE EXCEEDS the BIRTH RATE, natural growth is NEGATIVE, so the population DECLINES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. Population change = births − deaths + net migration. 2. Migration can change a region's population even if births equal deaths. Which is/are correct?
solution: BOTH are correct: POPULATION CHANGE = births − deaths + NET MIGRATION (1), and MIGRATION alone can change population even when births equal deaths (2). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A favourable sex ratio and high literacy generally indicate:
options: Better social development and status of women
solution: A FAVOURABLE SEX RATIO and HIGH LITERACY indicate BETTER SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT and improved STATUS of WOMEN. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following regions is likely to be densely populated?
options: The Ganga plains with fertile soil and water
solution: The GANGA PLAINS, with FERTILE SOIL and WATER, are DENSELY populated. Deserts, high mountains and dense forests are sparse. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The availability of minerals attracts population because:
options: Mining and related industries create jobs
solution: MINERALS attract population because MINING and RELATED INDUSTRIES create JOBS and economic opportunities. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Human beings are called the 'ultimate resource' because they:
options: Use their skills to turn other things into useful resources
solution: Humans are the ULTIMATE RESOURCE because they USE their SKILLS and KNOWLEDGE to TRANSFORM other things into useful resources. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following would LOWER the quality of a nation's human resources?
options: Poor education, ill health and lack of skills
solution: POOR EDUCATION, ILL HEALTH, and LACK of SKILLS LOWER the quality of human resources. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The uneven distribution of the world's population means that:
options: Some areas are crowded while vast areas are almost empty
solution: The UNEVEN distribution means SOME areas are CROWDED while VAST areas are almost EMPTY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following statements about migration is TRUE?
options: Migration redistributes population, increasing it in some areas and decreasing it in others
Migration has no effect on population
Migration only reduces total world population
solution: MIGRATION REDISTRIBUTES population — INCREASING it where people move to and DECREASING it where they leave. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'demographic transition' describes how, as a country develops, it moves from:
options: High birth and death rates to low birth and death rates
solution: The DEMOGRAPHIC TRANSITION describes the shift from HIGH birth and death rates to LOW birth and death rates as a country develops. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Overpopulation — too many people for resources 2. Underpopulation — too few people to use resources fully 3. Optimum population — best balance. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE match: OVERPOPULATION → too many for resources; UNDERPOPULATION → too few to use resources; OPTIMUM → best balance. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A country with a large elderly population may face challenges such as:
options: Higher spending on pensions and healthcare with a smaller workforce
solution: A large ELDERLY population raises spending on PENSIONS and HEALTHCARE while the WORKFORCE shrinks. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a geographical factor discouraging dense settlement?
solution: STEEP MOUNTAINS and HARSH CLIMATE DISCOURAGE dense settlement. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The birth rate and death rate are both expressed per:
solution: BIRTH and DEATH rates are expressed PER 1000 people PER YEAR. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A high literacy rate contributes to human resource development by:
options: Producing a skilled, informed and more employable workforce
solution: HIGH LITERACY produces a SKILLED, INFORMED, and more EMPLOYABLE workforce, aiding human resource development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between resources and population?
options: People become a valuable resource when their abilities are developed and used
Population has no link to resources
solution: PEOPLE become a VALUABLE RESOURCE when their ABILITIES are DEVELOPED and USED productively. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The main way to convert a large population into an asset is through:
options: Investment in education, health and skills
solution: A large population becomes an ASSET through INVESTMENT in EDUCATION, HEALTH, and SKILLS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Human Resources' is that:
options: People, when healthy, educated and skilled, are a nation's greatest resource
Population has no effect on development
solution: The chapter emphasises that a healthy, educated and skilled population is the most valuable resource of any nation.
